page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t6-c1m2.large is an entry-level, burstable virtual machine instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8269CY core with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core. It does not include any local storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate that this instance is designed for low-intensity workloads. In stress-ng testing, single-core CPU performance scored 1300.19 and multi-core scored 2402.69, both falling into the bottom 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests showed 186.46 GB/sec for cached small blocks and a lower 20.68 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. Geekbench results further highlight these constraints, with a single-core score of 1045.0 and a multi-core score of 1850.0.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.t6-c1m2.large is its burstable CPU allocation model, which limits sustained high-CPU utilization. Additionally, the instance operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 0 Gbps and lacks bundled local storage. However, this resource profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads with intermittent activity, as users avoid paying for idle, dedicated compute capacity.

This instance is best suited for lightweight, non-critical applications that experience sporadic traffic or require minimal background processing. Suitable workloads include basic static web serving, small-scale Redis caching, development or testing environments, and simple microservices that do not demand continuous high-performance compute or high network throughput.
